title: Go 1.27.0 toolchain: 6 reachable net/http standard library vulnerabilities fixed in Go 1.27.2
evidence: Verified: govulncheck on backend/ with go1.27.0 (saved in .forge/tmp/delivery/review/govulncheck.txt) reports 6 vulnerabilities reachable from our code, all fixed in go1.27.2: GO-2026-6617 (HTTP/2 HPACK encoder race, server crash), GO-2026-6613 (HTTP/1 desync after 2xx CONNECT), GO-2026-6612 (HTTP/2 double flow-control refund), GO-2026-6611 (CPU from repeated HTTP/2 initial window changes), GO-2026-6609 (no limit on parsed Range headers, reached through http.FileServer in internal/httpapi/routes.go), GO-2026-6603 (HTTP/2 memory exhaustion via Trailer headers). Traces go through cmd/server/main.go (http.Server.Serve/Shutdown) and internal/httpapi (middleware, routes). go.mod declared go 1.27.0 and the Dockerfile built with golang:1.27.0-bookworm.
impact: The shipped binary (Docker image and local builds) was exposed to denial of service (crash, CPU and memory exhaustion) and HTTP/1 desynchronization from untrusted clients.
precautions: Keep go.mod and the Dockerfile builder on the same patch release; rerun govulncheck (golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck) before each release, since new standard library advisories appear often.
verification: 2026-10-14: backend/go.mod raised to go 1.27.2 and the Dockerfile to golang:1.27.2-bookworm. go version in backend/ reports go1.27.2; govulncheck v1.8.0 ./... prints 'No vulnerabilities found.' (.forge/tmp/delivery/review/govulncheck-1.27.2.txt); go test passes (calculator 100 %, httpapi 95.4 %).
